## Record — the three-way split, measured

Full audit: `docs/audits/2026-09-hotcrm-handwritten-test-split.md` in #15431 (draft,
docs-only). It carries the per-file table (169 rows), the describe-level detail for
the 22 files that straddle buckets, and the method. Summary here.

Read-only against `objectstack-ai/hotcrm` at `71a3452`. **Every one of the 169 files
was read; nothing was classified by filename.** hotcrm was not modified and no test
was deleted, rewritten or reclassified in place.

### 1 + 2. Bucket totals, and the subtraction

| bucket | lines | share | ~tokens |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| **(1)** platform should derive it, hand-written today | **20,505** | 29.5% | 129,752 |
| **(2)** genuinely the app's own business judgement | **28,242** | 40.7% | 208,252 |
| **(3)** grey zone — platform behaviour, app carries the cost | **15,265** | 22.0% | 97,972 |
| **(4)** undecided | **5,407** | 7.8% | 30,610 |
| total | 69,419 | 100% | 466,587 |

Bucket (1) by derivation family — this split *is* the roadmap, so it is not folded away:

| family | lines | ~tokens |
|:--|--:|--:|
| (1f) docs-to-metadata consistency | 9,851 | 59,892 |
| (1a) metadata referential integrity | 4,344 | 29,297 |
| (1b) predicate totality and dialect | 3,415 | 21,857 |
| (1d) i18n completeness | 1,078 | 6,314 |
| (1c) authorization / sharing coverage | 968 | 6,968 |
| (1e) liveness (declared-but-inert) | 849 | 5,424 |

**(1) minus already-derived = 20,505 lines. The subtraction is zero.**

`derive.ts` + `rls.ts` derive exactly two app-agnostic families: per-object CRUD
round-trip type fidelity, and the RLS "you cannot write what you cannot read"
invariant fanned out per declared position. Neither corresponds to any bucket-(1)
test in hotcrm — there is no per-object CRUD round-trip test anywhere in its 160
files, and the RLS prover asks a runtime question where (1c) asks a static one.
(The package's other three exports — `checkLedger`, `checkReadCoercion`,
`checkDateBucketParity` — derive nothing from an app's metadata; they are platform
and driver conformance helpers, so they subtract nothing either.)

And, more bluntly: **hotcrm does not depend on `@objectstack/verify` at all.** It is
absent from `package.json`; `deriveCrudCases` / `runCrudVerification` / `runRlsProofs`
return zero hits across the repository. hotcrm's own `pnpm verify` is a locally
composed script that never invokes the platform's derived proofs.

**On the #15210 hypothesis — the history does not support it.** Every bucket-(1)
file was added between 2026-07-27 and 2026-08-17; #15210 was filed 2026-09-04, three
to six weeks later, and describes a *multi-package* composed config that a
single-package app like hotcrm cannot reach. The honest reading is simpler than
"the derived half could not be trusted": **the derived half was never offered to
this app.**

### 3. The derivation roadmap, heaviest first

1. **docs-to-metadata roster consistency** — 9,851 lines / ~59,892 tokens. Nearly
   half of bucket (1), and the family furthest outside `os verify`'s current remit:
   it needs the docs corpus as a second input, which the platform does not read today.
2. **metadata referential integrity** — 4,344 / ~29,297. Resolve every name a page,
   view, action, nav entry, dashboard, dataset, import mapping, skill or AI binding
   mentions. `os validate` checks shape; nothing checks the names inside it. Closest
   to what the platform already does — the cheapest first win.
3. **predicate totality and dialect** — 3,415 / ~21,857. Every authored CEL predicate
   returns a verdict for every record shape its trigger can hand it. Four files, all
   written as explicit "HOUSE RULE" suites because the failure is silent.
4. **i18n completeness** — 1,078 / ~6,314.
5. **authorization / sharing coverage** — 968 / ~6,968. Explicit-allow means an
   ungranted object is denied for everyone, admins included.
6. **liveness / declared-but-inert** — 849 / ~5,424. The platform already owns this
   concept for its own spec (ADR-0049, the liveness ledger); this is the same
   discipline applied to an app's metadata, hand-rolled.

### 4. The honest reading of the size claim

Token figures use hotcrm's **own** ratchet rule (`check-source-token-ratchet.mjs`
`stripComments`, blank-stripped, `chars / 4`). Running that script unmodified
reproduces its published `authored total ~135,830`, which is the check that the same
rule is being applied here.

| reading | ~tokens | vs. 150k |
|:--|--:|:--|
| `src` as the ratchet scopes it | 135,830 | fits |
| all of `src` (adding translations + seed data) | 229,022 | 1.5x |
| **`src` + the tests the app cannot avoid — floor** | **344,082** | **2.3x** |
| `src` + everything still hand-written after (1) is derived — ceiling | 472,664 | 3.2x |
| everything in `src` and `test` today | 695,609 | 4.6x |

**The number to quote is ~344,000 tokens** — `src` at 135,830 plus bucket (2) at
208,252 — and that floor already assumes the platform derives all of (1) *and*
absorbs every last line of (3), the most generous assumption available. It is 2.3x
the claim and does not fit one context window. An agent holding the app whole at
135,830 tokens holds the metadata and none of the 208,252 tokens that say what the
metadata must do.

`test/` at 466,587 tokens is **3.4x** the authored `src` surface the claim is
measured on. Of its 69,419 raw lines, 22,953 are comment and 5,947 blank — 40,519
execute.

I did **not** split bucket (3) into absorbable and permanent, because that line is
not measurable from the test text — it depends on roadmap decisions not yet made. So
the app's unavoidable test surface is reported as a range, 208,252 to 306,224 tokens.
What can be said precisely: **4,069 lines are unambiguously absorbable** — the
harness family (`helpers/flow-harness`, `helpers/hook-harness`,
`helpers/action-sandbox`, `helpers/tenancy-probe`, plus the four suites that exist
only to prove those stand-ins have not drifted from the engine). Every line of it
exists because the platform ships no first-party test harness.

### Corrections to the starting hypothesis

- **`hooks-runtime-service.test.ts` (1,503) is (2), not (3)** — the one real miss,
  and the largest file in the guess set. The stated reason ("inside the platform's
  own sandbox") describes `action-sandbox.test.ts`. This file imports the
  hand-written `helpers/hook-harness`, calls `hook.handler(ctx)` with the closure
  intact, and boots no sandbox and no engine. It asserts the 8-hour SLA clock, what
  a guest submission may state, contract and campaign validation — app policy.
- **`sharing-coverage.test.ts` (1,309) is 90% a docs test** — bucket right (1),
  family surprising: 1,178 lines are (1f), only 131 are (1c). Five of its eight
  describes check the admin docs' OWD, sharing-rules and related-list tables against
  the app in every locale. The name reads as authorization.
- `action-sandbox.test.ts` (976) — **(3) confirmed**.
- `metadata-references.test.ts` (1,288) — **(1) confirmed** (1,188 (1a) + 60 (1b) +
  a 40-line retired-persona tail that is (2)).
- `docs-view-rosters.test.ts` (1,095) and `i18n-references.test.ts` (866) — **(1)
  confirmed**. Note 432 of docs-view-rosters' 1,095 lines are its file-level comment.
- `quote-discount-ceiling.test.ts` (898) — **(2) confirmed**.
- `case-assignment.test.ts` (897) — mostly (2), but 214 lines measure a platform
  premise (what the transfer gate can see of a `beforeInsert` `owner_id` stamp).
- `win-loss-capture.test.ts` (857) — mostly (2); 62 lines are the same assertion
  re-run on real SQLite only because driver storage shapes differ.

**Bucket (1) is 4.5x the at-a-glance guess** (20,505 vs 4,558), and its two heaviest
families appear nowhere in the starting set.

### The undecided bucket, and why

- **(4t) repo and tooling hygiene — 5,172 lines.** Tests of hotcrm's *own* scripts,
  gates and CI config. Not business judgement, not metadata self-consistency, not
  platform behaviour: a fifth family the three-way taxonomy has no slot for. The
  platform will never derive these.
- **(4) genuinely ambiguous — 235 lines.** One describe:
  `forecast-current-quarter-view` / *"no view label promises a time scope its filter
  does not express"*. A platform could mechanically check that a view whose label
  carries a period token has a filter expressing it — but deciding that **"This
  Quarter"** *promises* a quarter means reading an app-authored string as language.
  Left undecided rather than forced.

The softest calls are named in the doc's Method section so they can be checked rather
than trusted — chiefly the (1f) family as a whole, which passes the card's test (no
business knowledge needed) but needs an input surface `os verify` does not read.
